Validates an object type tag (byte at +8 must equal 3), derives construction flags from tag bits 0x20000 and BYTE2 bit 0, builds X and Y interpolation coordinate tables via MemoryAllocation_53ec from the dimension pairs at dword indices 1046 and 1047, allocates two 16-byte staging buffers, iterates destination rows and columns, fetches source texels through vtable slot +4 and processes rows through vtable slot +8, applies weighted float interpolation using the coordinate blend factors, writes interpolated texels to the destination, frees the coordinate tables and staging buffers, and returns 0 on success or an HRESULT error code.

MemoryAllocation_53ec builds the X and Y interpolation coordinate tables from the source/destination dimension pairs at dword indices 1046 and 1047.
If either coordinate table allocation returns null, execution jumps to cleanup and the function returns -2147024882.

sub_5008C2 initialises the staged vector elements using the element constructor sub_5007EC.
If the first staging buffer is null, execution jumps to cleanup returning -2147024882.
A second staging buffer of 32 bytes per element is allocated and element-constructed via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper and sub_5008C2/sub_5007EC.
If the second staging buffer is null, execution jumps to cleanup returning -2147024882.
Nested do-while loops over the destination rows (index 1047) and columns (index 1046) resample every destination texel.
Source data is fetched through the vtable method at slot +4 and the per-row processing step is driven through the vtable method at slot +8.
Weighted float interpolation combines the coordinate-table blend factors with the four source texel channels (two x two bilinear taps).
The four interpolated float channels are written to the destination buffer element.
FreeWrapper_7bcf releases the two coordinate tables and the two staging buffers before returning.
Returns 0 on success, -2147467259 on tag mismatch, and -2147024882 when a table or staging allocation fails.

functions.name: CreateVertexBlendBufferWithFreelist
functions.summary: Builds a weighted-blend vertex staging pipeline. Guards on matching depth (offset 4192) on the source and destination objects, allocates coordinate remap tables for both dimensions via ComplexMemoryAllocationWithFloatComputation, allocates a vertex buffer whose elements are zero-initialised and freed through registered callbacks, builds a source contribution table, accumulates weighted source floats into destination vertices through an indirect vtable method, and recycles released vertex slots through a free list. Frees every allocated staging structure before returning the status code.

Call ComplexMemoryAllocationWithFloatComputation with the offset 4184 dimension sizes of both objects to build the first coordinate remap table.
Call ComplexMemoryAllocationWithFloatComputation with the offset 4188 dimension sizes of both objects to build the second coordinate remap table.
Guard that both remap table allocations succeeded; otherwise fall through to the error return -2147467259.
Allocate the staging buffer header with OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper(12 * elementCount + 4); the first dword stores the element count and the element array starts one dword later.
Construct the vertex buffer element array via NTimeCallbackLoopWithSEH_a6eb using TripleDwordZeroInit as the per-element initialiser and FreeWrapper as the per-element free callback.
Allocate the source contribution table with OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper(16 * sourceCount) and construct its elements with sub_5008C2 using sub_5007EC as the element constructor.

Iterate the first remap table entries and increment the reference count stored at offset 8 of each addressed vertex buffer slot (12-byte stride).

Iterate the second remap table entries; for each slot with a null element either reuse a freed slot from the free list or allocate and construct a new one via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper and sub_5008C2/sub_5007EC, zeroing it with memset.
Invoke the indirect vtable method at *(*(*v2) + 4) on the destination object to emit the accumulated vertices.
Weighted blend accumulation loop: for each source/destination pair multiply source floats by a weight and accumulate them into the destination vertex components (stride 16 bytes per vertex).
Decrement the per-slot reference count; when it reaches zero invoke the release vtable method at *(*(*v2[1]) + 8) and push the slot onto the free list.
Conditionally free the vertex buffer via ConditionalFree_2ee5 when the element array is present.
Free the two coordinate remap tables and the source contribution table via FreeWrapper_7bcf.
Return the status code v38 (0 on success, -2147467259 on allocation/guard failure, -2147024882 when the staging buffer is absent).
Called by D3DContextInit (0x005063A5) to create the vertex buffer during D3D context initialisation.

functions.name: D3DTextureSurfaceLockCopy
functions.summary: D3D surface copy helper: tears down existing render resources, queries the input surface (a3) description, validates the optional source rect (a5) against the surface dimensions, optionally probes hardware capability via GetDesc, creates a compatible surface sized to the source, copies pixel data (CopyRects) or locks the destination surface rect (LockRect) with per-format (compressed vs. plain) alignment, and fills the output descriptor a2 with pitch, format, dimensions, rect and ownership fields. this+0x8 holds the destination surface, this+0xC the source surface, this+0x0 the control flags (a7) and this+0x4 the input surface pointer (a3). Returns 0 on success or a D3D error code.

operations.description: RenderResourceTeardown(this) releases existing render resources owned by the copier before re-locking.
Dispatch the vtable+32 method on the input surface a3, which fills the description locals (v25 format and v26..v29 dimensions).
When a5 is provided, copy the four rect coordinates and validate them against the surface dimensions v28/v29; an out-of-range rect returns a fixed D3D error code.
Derive control flags: v43 = (a7 & 1) == 0 and no partial rect; v45 marks a partial rect; the rect defaults to the full surface when a5 is null.

Capability gate: when a7 bit 0x10000 is clear, run sub_500EAC(1), then GetDesc (vtable+28) on a3 with the unk_5AD4D0 descriptor buffer to decide whether the lock-copy path is supported; fall back to reading a3[4] format bits when GetDesc fails, then sub_500EAC(0).
Compressed-format alignment: when the format code v25 belongs to the DXT-style compressed family, round width and height up to a 4-byte boundary ((dims+3) & ~3); otherwise keep them as-is.

Create a compatible surface: dispatch the vtable+108 method on the source surface (pointer at this+0xC, vtable at *(this+0xC)+0x0) with the aligned dimensions, format and a result slot at this+0x8; a negative HRESULT aborts.
Optional CopyRects: when the fast path is not selected, dispatch the vtable+112 method on the source surface (this+0xC) to copy into the compatible surface.

Hardware support probe: when the fast path is active, run sub_500EAC(1), GetDesc (vtable+28) on a3 with the unk_5AD4C0 descriptor buffer, and if the queried support check reports true OR the 0x2000 flag into the LockRect flags; release the descriptor and run sub_500EAC(0).

Per-format rect alignment before locking: DXT-family formats align the rect coordinates to 4 bytes, the odd-aligned format family to 2 bytes, otherwise the rect is used as-is, clamping against the surface dimensions.

LockRect on the destination surface: dispatch the vtable+36 method (field *(*(this+0x8)+0x0)+0x24) on the destination surface pointer (this+0x8, vtable at *(this+0x8)+0x0) with the aligned source rect and computed flags; a negative HRESULT propagates.
Fill the output descriptor a2: zero sentinel slots, store pitch, format, dimensions, the four rect coordinates, the extra a4/a6 values, and set the 1-valued marker fields.
Persist state on the copier: store the input surface pointer a3 into this+0x4 and the control flags a7 into this+0x0.
Return 0 on success; propagate any negative HRESULT from the surface vtable calls.
Invoked by NetworkPacketSendReceive (0050070d) and SurfaceBlitOperation (0050099c) to lock and copy texture surface data.

functions.name: ComplexDestructorWithLoop
